enclitic particle of asseveration, often rendered "surely" or "indeed"

enclitic particle having the force of asseveration and serving to confirm the statement, so that it can generally be rendered by Latin sane, utique. Not infrequently it is joined with other particles: ἀλλὰ τοι [but indeed] (Pers. 795. Ag. 1303. Suppl. 952), γάρ τοι [for indeed] (Ag. 1040. Fr. 282), γέ τοι [at least indeed] (Ag. 1001), δέ τοι [and indeed] (Pr. 1021. Sept. 80. Pers. 506. Ch. 542. Suppl. 393 688. Ag. 974 1444 1659), εἴ τοι [if indeed] (Suppl. 387), ἤ τοι [or indeed] (Ag. 662 849. Ch. 497) [ἢ τἄν Sept. 552], μή τοι [not indeed] (of prohibition Pr. 436 625). On other particles combined with τοι we have spoken under καίτοι, μέντοι, μήτοι, οὔτοι.
